title: The Complete Passive Reconnaissance Workflow
description: This diagram shows the full professional passive reconnaissance workflow from client brief to active testing authorisation. Each node is a phase or decision point. The edges show the sequence and the outputs that flow from each phase into the next. The critical decision diamond — 'Critical finding during passive recon?' — shows the immediate escalation path that runs parallel to the normal workflow.

nodes.label: Client Brief
nodes.sublabel: Engagement kickoff: scope document, RoE, timeline

nodes.label: Phase 1: Scope Review
nodes.sublabel: Read scope completely. Extract: in-scope assets, exclusions, RoE, emergency contacts, timeline

nodes.label: Reconnaissance Plan
nodes.sublabel: Asset list, priority order, technique authorisations, documentation standards

nodes.label: Phase 2: Passive Information Gathering
nodes.sublabel: WHOIS → DNS Enumeration → Search Engine Recon → OSINT

nodes.label: DNS Enumeration
nodes.sublabel: All 8 record types, subdomain discovery, zone transfer attempt

nodes.label: Search Engine Recon
nodes.sublabel: Google Dorking, robots.txt, Shodan, GitHub, Wayback Machine

nodes.label: Critical Finding?
nodes.sublabel: Active breach? Unauthenticated live data? Out-of-scope critical exposure?

nodes.label: Immediate Escalation
nodes.sublabel: Contact client emergency contact NOW — do not wait for final report

nodes.label: Phase 3: Intelligence Analysis
nodes.sublabel: Correlate findings. Confirm multi-source. Build infrastructure picture.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Attack Surface Map
nodes.sublabel: Critical / High / Medium / Low tiers. Entry point prioritisation.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Recon Report
nodes.sublabel: Documented findings with source, evidence, severity, recommended action

nodes.label: Active Testing Begins
nodes.sublabel: Targeted scanning, exploitation — guided by attack surface map

caption: The critical decision diamond appears during the passive gathering phase — not at the end. Critical findings (active breach, unauthenticated live data, credentials in active use) trigger immediate escalation to the client emergency contact. This runs parallel to the investigation, not at the end of it. Everything else accumulates into the intelligence analysis phase, flows into the attack surface map, and produces the reconnaissance report that is delivered before active testing begins. Active testing is the final phase — not the first.
